people.descriptorSuggestion: Jin Tribal Chief and Military Commander

claims.action: When the Liao marched to recover Haizhou he went with the tribal chief Maji to its relief, met a heavy enemy force on the road, fought hard, and took more than a thousand heads.
claims.sourceText: 遼人來取海州，從勃堇麻吉往援，道遇重敵，力戰，斬首千級。

claims.action: Bahei, however, stood high in the lineage and nursed designs of his own; he could not be brought to heel.
claims.sourceText: 而跋黑以屬尊，蓄異謀，不可制。

people.descriptorSuggestion: Nahana Clansman and Elder Brother of Azu’a

claims.action: Earlier Azu'a, younger brother of Saba of the Nahana tribe on the Yehui River, had quarreled over a tribal post and failed to obtain justice. He came in submission to Muzong.
claims.sourceText: 初，耶悔水納喝部撒八之弟曰阿注阿，與人爭部族官，不得直，來歸穆宗。

claims.office: Staff Officer of the Marshal’s Office and head of a meng’an
Associate Military Governor of Kaiyuan Army
Military Affairs Judge of the Zhongdu Circuit
Associate Military Governor of Anhua Army

Junior Household Master of the Heir Apparent, Military Governor of Kaiyuan, Basu Commander, and Northwest Pacification Commissioner

claims.statement: Incorrupt, loyal, upright, decisive, and praised in every assignment

claims.qualitative: Died after serving as Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit

claims.action: Pucha moved from the Meijian River in the Upper Capital to settle at Tiande.
claims.sourceText: 蒲查，自上京梅堅河徙屯天德。

claims.action: He first served as a staff officer of the Marshal's Office. Dispatched to the four quarters he acquitted himself well, and in investigation he always reached the truth. He headed a meng'an.
claims.sourceText: 初為元帥府紮也，使于四方稱職，按事能得其實，領猛安。

claims.action: During Huangtong he became Associate Military Governor of Kaiyuan Army. His scouts were strict and the frontier knew no trouble.
claims.sourceText: 皇統間，除同知開遠軍節度使，斥候嚴整，邊境無事。

claims.action: Early in Zhenglong he became Military Affairs Judge of the Zhongdu circuit.
claims.sourceText: 正隆初，為中都路兵馬判官。

claims.action: Bandits were rife about the capital. Pucha took more than forty ringleaders, and the people breathed easier.
claims.sourceText: 是時，京畿多盜，蒲查捕得大盜四十余人，百姓稍安。

claims.action: He was made Associate Military Governor of Anhua Army.

In Dading 2 he led the campaign ten-thousand-household force as prefect of Pizhou and director of military affairs, commanded the local ten-thousand households and nine garrisoned meng'an armies, served as military governor of Changwu Army, and as Deputy Commander-in-Chief of Shandong.
claims.sourceText: 大定二年，領行軍萬戶，充邳州刺史、知軍事，領本州萬戶，管所屯九猛安軍，昌武軍節度使，山東副都統。

claims.action: When Sagai marched south, the Marshal's Office appointed Pucha acting deputy commander-in-chief.
claims.sourceText: 撒改南征，元帥府以蒲查行副統事。

claims.action: He entered court as Junior Household Master of the Heir Apparent, became Military Governor of Kaiyuan Army, inherited his paternal uncle Gunan's meng'an, served as overall commander of Basu and as Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit, and died.
claims.sourceText: 入為太子少詹事，再遷開遠軍節度使，襲伯父骨赧猛安，曆婆速路兵馬都總管，西北路招討使，卒。

claims.action: Pucha was incorrupt, loyal, and upright, decisive in action, and praised in every post entrusted to him.
claims.sourceText: 蒲查性廉潔忠直，臨事能斷，凡被任使，無不稱雲。

claims.action: Gushi, Bashi, and others of the Pucha tribe lured the troops into a city and trapped more than three hundred men.
claims.sourceText: 蒲察部故石、拔石等，誘其眾入城，陷三百餘人。

claims.action: Yehe came in submission together with Balai of his own division, Huduhua and Sidu of the Pucha on the Womin River, Antuan of the Wanyan on the Taishentebai River, and Huoligai of the Wendihen on the Tongmen River. From that time the Jin state grew still stronger.
claims.sourceText: 與同部人把裏勃堇，斡泯水蒲察部胡都化勃堇、廝都勃堇，泰神忒保水完顏部安團勃堇，統門水溫蒂痕部活裏蓋勃堇，俱來歸，金之為國，自此益大。

claims.action: In Mingchang 5 he was raised to Special Advancement with the posthumous name Zhongji, Loyal and Succoring, and together with Duke of Dai Huandu, Special Advancement Hezhe, Grand Master of the Palace Penna, and Bearer of the Triple Staff Bada was granted collateral sacrifice in Shizu's temple.
claims.sourceText: 明昌五年，贈特進，諡忠濟，與代國公歡都、特進劾者、開府儀同三司盆納、儀同三司拔達，俱配享世祖廟廷。

units.zh: 古者太史掌敘邦國之世次，辨其姓氏，別其昭穆，尚失。
units.en: Even in ancient times the Grand Historian who ordered the ages of the realms, sorted clan names, and marked senior from junior lines could not keep the record whole.
units.literal: In antiquity the Grand Historian kept the generations of the states, distinguished their surnames, and separated zhao from mu—and still there were lapses.

units.zh: 金人初起完毅十二部，其後皆以部為氏，史臣記錄有稱「宗室」者，有稱完顏者。
units.en: The Jin first gathered in the twelve Wanyi tribes, then took each tribe as a clan name. Court historians sometimes wrote "Imperial Clan", sometimes Wanyan.
units.literal: When the Jin people first arose in the twelve tribes of Wanyi, afterward all took their tribe as surname; in the historians' records some are called "Imperial Clan", some Wanyan.

units.zh: 稱完顏者亦有二焉，有同姓完顏，蓋疏族，若石土門、迪古乃是也；
units.en: "Wanyan" itself split two ways: same-surname Wanyan were really distant kin, men like Shitumen and Digunai;
units.literal: Those called Wanyan also fall into two kinds: same-surname Wanyan, who were in fact collateral kin—Shitumen and Digunai are examples;

units.zh: 有異姓完顏，蓋部人，若歡都是也。
units.en: different-surname Wanyan were really tribesmen, men like Huandu.
units.literal: and different-surname Wanyan, who were in fact men of the tribe—Huandu is an example.

units.zh: 大定以前稱「宗室」，明昌以後避睿宗諱稱「內族」，其實一而已，書名不書氏，其制如此。
units.en: Before Dading they were called "Imperial Clan"; after Mingchang, to avoid the taboo on Ruizong, "Inner Kin"—the same group in fact. Registers record personal names, not clan names; that was the rule.
units.literal: Before the Dading era they were called "Imperial Clan"; after Mingchang, to avoid the taboo on Ruizong they were called "Inner Kin"—in substance one and the same. The annals give personal names, not clan names; such was the rule.

units.zh: 宣宗詔宗室皆稱完顏，不復識別焉。
units.en: Emperor Xuanzong ordered that all imperial kin take the name Wanyan, and the old distinctions ceased.
units.literal: Emperor Xuanzong decreed that all of the imperial clan should be called Wanyan, and no further distinction was made.

units.zh: 大定、泰和之間，袒免以上親皆有屬籍，以敘授官，大功以上，薨卒輟朝，親親之道行焉。
units.en: From Dading through Taihe, relatives within tan-mian degree and nearer were entered in the clan rolls and ranked for appointment; when one within da-gong degree or nearer died, court paused in mourning—kinship was honored in deed.
units.literal: Between Dading and Taihe, kin within the degree of tan-mian mourning and closer all had household registers, by which offices were assigned; for kin within the degree of da-gong mourning and closer, death halted court audiences—the way of cherishing kin was practiced.

units.zh: 貞祐以後，譜牒散失，大概僅存，不可殫悉，今掇其可次第者著於篇。
units.en: After Zhenyou the pedigree books were lost; a broken outline alone remains, too fragmentary to exhaust. Here I collect what can still be sequenced and place it in these pages.
units.literal: After Zhenyou the genealogical registers were scattered and lost; only a rough outline survives, and it cannot be set forth in full. Now I gather what can be ordered by generation and set it down in this chapter.

units.zh: 其上無所系、下無所承者，不能盡錄也。
units.en: Lines that attach to nothing above and hand down to nothing below cannot be entered in full.
units.literal: Those with no tie above and no succession below cannot all be recorded.

units.literal: At right: four sons of Hailing.

units.zh: 右睿宗子，與世宗凡二人。
units.en: Listed at right: sons of Ruizong—two in all, with Shizong.
units.literal: At right: sons of Ruizong—two in all, with Shizong.

units.zh: 右世宗子，與顯宗、衞紹王凡十人。
units.en: Listed at right: sons of Shizong—with Xianzong and Wei Shaowang, ten in all.
units.literal: At right: sons of Shizong—with Xianzong and Wei Shaowang, ten in all.

units.zh: 右顯宗子，與章宗、宣宗凡七人。
units.en: Listed at right: sons of Xianzong—with Zhangzong and Xuanzong, seven in all.
units.literal: At right: sons of Xianzong—with Zhangzong and Xuanzong, seven in all.

units.en: Listed at right: six sons of Zhangzong.
units.literal: At right: six sons of Zhangzong.

units.zh: 右紹王子，史稱六子，可以名見者四人。
units.en: Listed at right: sons of Shaowang; the histories say six sons, of whom four can be named in the record.
units.literal: At right: sons of Shaowang; the histories say six sons, of whom four can be named in the record.

units.zh: 右宣宗子，與末帝凡四人。
units.en: Listed at right: sons of Xuanzong—with the Last Emperor, four in all.
units.literal: At right: sons of Xuanzong—with the Last Emperor, four in all.

units.zh: 他書載守純子三人，可以名見者二人。
units.en: Other books record that Shouchun had three sons, of whom two can be named in the record.
units.literal: Other books record that Shouchun had three sons, of whom two can be named in the record.

units.en: Agunai (elder brother of the First Ancestor).
units.literal: Agunai (elder brother of the First Ancestor).

units.en: Hezhu (in Liao held Chen and Fu prefectures).
units.literal: Hezhu (in Liao held Chen and Fu prefectures).

units.en: Buhui (Military Commissioner of the Shuntian Army).
units.literal: Buhui (Military Commissioner of the Shuntian Army).

units.en: Baohuoli (younger brother of the First Ancestor).
units.literal: Baohuoli (younger brother of the First Ancestor).

units.zh: 迪古乃（同中書門下平章事。）
units.en: Digunai (Fellow Associate Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery).
units.literal: Digunai (Fellow Associate Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery).

units.zh: 婆盧火（安帝五代孫。泰州都統。）
units.en: Boluohuo (fifth-generation descendant of Emperor An; Commander-in-Chief of Taizhou).
units.literal: Boluohuo (fifth-generation descendant of Emperor An; Commander-in-Chief of Taizhou).

units.zh: 胡特孛山（婆盧火族兄弟。）
杲（本名撒離喝。行臺尚書、左丞相。）
units.en: Gao (born Saliehe; Mobile-Administration Minister of the Secretariat, Left Chancellor).
units.literal: Gao (born Saliehe; Mobile-Administration Minister of the Secretariat, Left Chancellor).

units.zh: 什古（昭祖曾孫。東京留守。）
units.en: Shigu (great-grandson of Zhao Zu; Eastern Capital Defender).
units.literal: Shigu (great-great-grandson of Zhao Zu; Eastern Capital Defender).

units.zh: 崇成（昭祖玄孫。武軍都指揮使。）
units.en: Chongcheng (great-great-grandson of Zhao Zu; Commander of the Martial Army).
units.literal: Chongcheng (great-great-great-grandson of Zhao Zu; Commander of the Martial Army).

units.zh: 冶訶（係出景祖。銀青光祿大夫。）
units.en: Yekhe (line traced to Jing Zu; Silver Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness).
units.literal: Yekhe (line traced to Jing Zu; Silver Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness).

units.en: Guhua (Military Commissioner of the Tiande Army).
units.literal: Guhua (Military Commissioner of the Tiande Army).

units.zh: 阿魯補（係出景祖。行臺左丞相。）
units.en: Alubu (line traced to Jing Zu; Mobile-Administration Left Chancellor).
units.literal: Alubu (line traced to Jing Zu; Mobile-Administration Left Chancellor).

units.en: Fang (Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs).
units.literal: Fang (Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs).

units.zh: 胡八魯（穆宗孫，寧州刺史。）
units.en: Hubalu (grandson of Muzong; Prefect of Ningzhou).
units.literal: Hubalu (grandson of Muzong; Prefect of Ningzhou).

units.en: Qi (Military Commissioner of the Lishe Army).
units.literal: Qi (Military Commissioner of the Lishe Army).

units.zh: 拔離速（宗室子。元帥左監軍。）
units.en: Balisu (imperial clansman; Marshal Left Supervisor of the Army).
units.literal: Balisu (imperial clansman; Marshal Left Supervisor of the Army).

units.zh: 銀术可（拔離族子。同中書門下平章事。）
units.en: Yinshuake (kinsman of the Balisu clan; Fellow Associate Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery).
units.literal: Yinshuake (kinsman of the Balisu clan; Fellow Associate Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery).

units.zh: 麻吉（銀术可弟。銀青光祿大夫。）
units.en: Maji (younger brother of Yinshuake; Silver Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness).
units.literal: Maji (younger brother of Yinshuake; Silver Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness).

units.zh: 宗賢（本名阿魯。太祖從姪。婆速路兵馬都緫管。）
units.en: Zongxian (born Alu; Taizu's nephew by the collateral line; Commander of the Bosu-route military).
units.literal: Zongxian (born Alu; Taizu's nephew by the collateral line; Commander of the Bosu-route military).

units.zh: 右諸宗室可譜者凡十一族，雖稱系出某帝，而不能世次，不譜於各帝之下，所以慎也。
units.en: Listed at right: of the imperial kin who can be entered in a pedigree, eleven clans in all; though they are said to stem from a given emperor, their generations cannot be fixed, so they are not entered under each emperor's line — hence the caution.
units.literal: At right: of the imperial kin who can be entered in a pedigree, eleven clans in all; though they are said to stem from a given emperor, their generations cannot be fixed, so they are not entered under each emperor's line — hence the caution.

units.zh: 遼人來取海州，從勃堇麻吉往援，道遇重敵，力戰，斬首千級。
units.en: When the Liao marched to recover Haizhou he went with the tribal chief Maji to its relief, met a heavy enemy force on the road, fought hard, and took more than a thousand heads.
units.literal: When the Liao came to retake Haizhou, he followed the tribal chief Maji to relieve it; on the road they met a strong enemy and fought fiercely, beheading more than a thousand.

units.zh: 可喜 阿瑣 宗敏本名阿魯補 元宗峻子，本名常勝
units.en: Kexi, A Suo, Zong Min (born Alubu); Yuan, son of Zong Jun, born Changsheng.
units.literal: Kexi, A Suo, Zong Min (born Alubu); Yuan, son of Zong Jun, born Changsheng.

units.zh: 胙王元，景宣皇帝峻子也，本名常勝，為北京留守，弟查刺為安武軍節度使。
units.en: Yuan, Prince of Zu, son of the Jingxuan Emperor Jun, was born Changsheng. He served as regent at the Northern Capital; his brother Chaci was military commissioner of the Anwu Army.
units.literal: Yuan, Prince of Zu, was a son of the Jingxuan Emperor Jun; his original name was Changsheng. He was Northern Capital regent; his younger brother Chaci was military commissioner of the Anwu Army.

units.zh: 又曰：「蒲陽溫胙王元，外若愚訥，臨事明敏過人。
units.en: He went on: "Puyangwen—Prince of Zu Yuan—seemed slow and tongue-tied, yet in business he outshone everyone.
units.literal: He added: "Puyangwen, Prince of Zu Yuan—outwardly dull and slow of speech, yet in affairs keener than other men.

units.en: Your Majesty has only two brothers—Changsheng and Chaci.
units.literal: Your Majesty’s brothers are only Changsheng and Chaci.

units.zh: 元子育，本名合住，大定二十七年，自南京副留守遷大宗正丞，兼勸農副使。
units.en: Yuan’s son Yu, born Hezhu: in Dading year 27 he went from deputy regent at the Southern Capital to Grand Director of the Imperial Clan and Vice Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture.
units.literal: Yuan’s son Yu, original name Hezhu—in the twenty-seventh year of Dading he moved from deputy regent of the Southern Capital to Grand Director of the Imperial Clan, and concurrently Vice Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture.

units.zh: 皇統七年四月戊午，左副點檢蒲察阿虎特子尚主，進禮物，賜宴便殿。
units.en: In the fourth month of Huangtong year 7, day wuwu: the son of Left Vice Director of the Palace Inspection Bureau Pucha Ahute married a princess and brought wedding gifts; the emperor gave a feast in the Informal Hall.
units.literal: In the seventh year of Huangtong, on the day wuwu of the fourth month, the son of Left Vice Director of the Palace Inspection Bureau Pucha Ahute married the princess and presented wedding gifts; a feast was granted in the Informal Hall.

units.zh: 海陵篡立，追封常勝、查刺、阿楞官爵，親臨葬所致祭。
units.en: Once Hailing seized the throne he posthumously restored Changsheng, Chaci, and Aleng, and came in person to their graves to sacrifice.
units.literal: When Hailing usurped the throne he posthumously restored the offices and titles of Changsheng, Chaci, and Aleng, and in person came to their burials to offer sacrifice.

units.zh: 於是，乃殺常勝及其弟查刺，並殺特思。
units.en: Then they killed Changsheng and his brother Chaci, and killed Tesi too.
units.literal: Thereupon they killed Changsheng and his brother Chaci, and killed Tesi as well.

units.zh: 熙宗被酒，酌酒賜元，元不能飲，上怒，仗劍逼之，元逃去。
units.en: Xizong, already drunk, poured wine and pressed it on Yuan. Yuan could not drink. The emperor flew into a rage, sword in hand, and drove at him; Yuan fled.
units.literal: Xizong was drunk, poured wine and bestowed it on Yuan; Yuan could not drink—the sovereign grew angry, drew his sword and pressed him; Yuan fled.

units.zh: 命左丞宗憲召元，宗憲與元俱去，上益怒，是時戶部尚書宗禮在側，使之跪，手殺之。
units.en: He ordered Left Vice Director Zongxian to fetch Yuan; Zongxian left with him, and the emperor’s wrath only mounted. Minister of Revenue Zongli stood nearby—the emperor forced him to his knees and killed him himself.
units.literal: He ordered Left Vice Director Zongxian to summon Yuan; Zongxian went off with Yuan together—the sovereign grew still angrier. At that time Minister of Revenue Zongli was at his side; he made him kneel and killed him with his own hand.

units.zh: 而辯與秉德初意不在海陵，常勝乃熙宗之弟，辯答曰：「無胙王常勝乎。」
units.en: Bian and Bingde had not first thought of Hailing. Changsheng was Xizong’s own brother. Bian said: "What of the Prince of Zu, Changsheng?"
units.literal: But Bian and Bingde at first had not had Hailing in mind; Changsheng was Xizong’s younger brother—Bian answered: "Is there not the Prince of Zu, Changsheng?"

units.zh: 由是海陵謂胙王有人望，不除之將不得立，故心忌常勝並阿楞。
units.en: Thence Hailing reckoned the Prince of Zu held the people’s favor—without removing him he could not reign—and so he hated Changsheng and Aleng alike.
units.literal: From this Hailing judged that the Prince of Zu had the people’s regard—unless he were removed he could not be enthroned; therefore in his heart he envied Changsheng together with Aleng.

units.zh: 河南軍士孫進自稱「皇弟按察大王」，熙宗疑「皇弟」二字或在常勝也，使特思鞫之，無狀。
units.en: Sun Jin, a soldier in Henan, called himself "Younger Brother, Inspector King." Xizong wondered whether "younger brother" meant Changsheng and set Tesi to question him; nothing was proved.
units.literal: A soldier of the Henan army, Sun Jin, styled himself "Younger Brother, Inspector King"; Xizong suspected the words "younger brother" might point to Changsheng, and had Tesi interrogate him—no proof emerged.

units.zh: 海陵知熙宗有疑常勝心，因此可以除之，謂熙宗曰：「孫進反有端，不稱他人，乃稱皇弟大王。
units.en: Hailing saw that Xizong already doubted Changsheng and that here was his chance. He told Xizong: "Sun Jin’s revolt has a thread to pull—he named no one else but Younger Brother the King.
units.literal: Hailing knew Xizong already doubted Changsheng, and that by this he could remove him; he said to Xizong: "Sun Jin’s rebellion has a basis—he named no other man, only Younger Brother the King.

units.zh: 熙宗以為然，使唐括辯、蕭肄按問特思，特思自誣服，故出常勝罪。
units.en: Xizong agreed and set Tangguo Bian and Xiao Yi to press Tesi; Tesi confessed under torture, and Changsheng was condemned.
units.literal: Xizong thought it so, and had Tangguo Bian and Xiao Yi examine and question Tesi; Tesi falsely confessed, and thus the charge against Changsheng was established.

units.zh: 太祖諸孫中，惟胙王元天性賢者也。」
units.en: Of Taizu’s grandsons, only Prince of Zu Yuan was truly worthy by nature."
units.literal: Among the Taizu’s grandsons, only Prince of Zu Yuan was gifted with a worthy nature by Heaven."

units.zh: 朕于兄弟間，于元尤款密。」
units.en: Of all my brothers, none was dearer to me than Yuan."
units.literal: Among my brothers, toward Yuan I was especially close and intimate."

units.zh: 而跋黑以屬尊，蓄異謀，不可制。
units.en: Bahei, however, stood high in the lineage and nursed designs of his own; he could not be brought to heel.
units.literal: But Bahei, by reason of senior kinship, harbored other designs and could not be controlled.

units.zh: 初，耶悔水納喝部撒八之弟曰阿注阿，與人爭部族官，不得直，來歸穆宗。
units.en: Earlier Azu'a, younger brother of Saba of the Nahana tribe on the Yehui River, had quarreled over a tribal post and failed to obtain justice. He came in submission to Muzong.
units.literal: In the beginning Azu'a, younger brother of Saba of the Yehui Nahana tribe on the Yehui River, disputed a tribal office with another and did not obtain justice; he came to submit to Muzong.

units.zh: 列傳第六 ○歡都子 謀演 冶訶子 阿魯補 骨赧 訛古乃 蒲查
units.en: Biographies 6: Huandu and his son Mouyan; Yehe and his sons Alubu, Gunan, and Egunai; Sanda's son Pucha
units.literal: Biographies 6: Huandu and his son Mouyan; Yehe and his sons Alubu, Gunan, and Egunai; Sanda's son Pucha

units.zh: 初為元帥府紮也，使于四方稱職，按事能得其實，領猛安。
units.en: He first served as a staff officer of the Marshal's Office. Dispatched to the four quarters he acquitted himself well, and in investigation he always reached the truth. He headed a meng'an.
units.literal: At first he was a zha ye of the Marshal's Office; sent to the four quarters he performed his duties well; in investigating affairs he could get at the truth; he headed a meng'an.

units.zh: 皇統間，除同知開遠軍節度使，斥候嚴整，邊境無事。
units.en: During Huangtong he became Associate Military Governor of Kaiyuan Army. His scouts were strict and the frontier knew no trouble.
units.literal: During Huangtong he was made Associate Military Governor of Kaiyuan Army; his scouts were strict and orderly, and the frontier was untroubled.

units.zh: 正隆初，為中都路兵馬判官。
units.en: Early in Zhenglong he became Military Affairs Judge of the Zhongdu circuit.
units.literal: At the beginning of Zhenglong he became Military Affairs Judge of the Zhongdu circuit.

units.en: He was made Associate Military Governor of Anhua Army.
units.literal: He was changed to Associate Military Governor of Anhua Army.

units.zh: 大定二年，領行軍萬戶，充邳州刺史、知軍事，領本州萬戶，管所屯九猛安軍，昌武軍節度使，山東副都統。
units.en: In Dading 2 he led the campaign ten-thousand-household force as prefect of Pizhou and director of military affairs, commanded the local ten-thousand households and nine garrisoned meng'an armies, served as military governor of Changwu Army, and as Deputy Commander-in-Chief of Shandong.
units.literal: In Dading year 2 he led the campaign ten-thousand-household army, served as prefect of Pizhou and director of military affairs, headed the ten-thousand households of that prefecture, administered the nine meng'an armies garrisoned there, was military governor of Changwu Army, and Deputy Commander-in-Chief of Shandong.

units.zh: 撒改南征，元帥府以蒲查行副統事。
units.en: When Sagai marched south, the Marshal's Office appointed Pucha acting deputy commander-in-chief.
units.literal: When Sagai campaigned south, the Marshal's Office made Pucha acting deputy commander-in-chief.

units.zh: 入為太子少詹事，再遷開遠軍節度使，襲伯父骨赧猛安，曆婆速路兵馬都總管，西北路招討使，卒。
units.en: He entered court as Junior Household Master of the Heir Apparent, became Military Governor of Kaiyuan Army, inherited his paternal uncle Gunan's meng'an, served as overall commander of Basu and as Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit, and died.
units.literal: He entered the capital as Junior Household Master of the Heir Apparent, was again transferred to Military Governor of Kaiyuan Army, inherited his paternal uncle Gunan's meng'an, served successively as overall commander of Basu circuit forces and Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit, and died.

units.zh: 蒲查性廉潔忠直，臨事能斷，凡被任使，無不稱雲。
units.en: Pucha was incorrupt, loyal, and upright, decisive in action, and praised in every post entrusted to him.
units.literal: Pucha was by nature incorrupt, loyal, and upright; facing affairs he could decide; whenever entrusted with a mission, none failed to praise him.

units.zh: 蒲查，自上京梅堅河徙屯天德。
units.en: Pucha moved from the Meijian River in the Upper Capital to settle at Tiande.
units.literal: Pucha moved from the Meijian River in the Upper Capital to garrison at Tiande.

units.zh: 是時，京畿多盜，蒲查捕得大盜四十余人，百姓稍安。
units.en: Bandits were rife about the capital. Pucha took more than forty ringleaders, and the people breathed easier.
units.literal: At that time bandits were numerous in the capital region; Pucha captured more than forty major bandits, and the common people were somewhat at peace.

units.zh: 蒲察部故石、拔石等，誘其眾入城，陷三百餘人。
units.en: Gushi, Bashi, and others of the Pucha tribe lured the troops into a city and trapped more than three hundred men.
units.literal: Gushi, Bashi, and others of the Pucha tribe enticed their forces into the city and trapped more than three hundred men.

units.zh: 與同部人把裏勃堇，斡泯水蒲察部胡都化勃堇、廝都勃堇，泰神忒保水完顏部安團勃堇，統門水溫蒂痕部活裏蓋勃堇，俱來歸，金之為國，自此益大。
units.en: Yehe came in submission together with Balai of his own division, Huduhua and Sidu of the Pucha on the Womin River, Antuan of the Wanyan on the Taishentebai River, and Huoligai of the Wendihen on the Tongmen River. From that time the Jin state grew still stronger.
units.literal: Together with Balai, tribal chief of the same division, Huduhua and Sidu, tribal chiefs of the Pucha tribe on the Womin River, Antuan, tribal chief of the Wanyan tribe on the Taishentebai River, and Huoligai, tribal chief of the Wendihen tribe on the Tongmen River, they all came to submit; from this the Jin state grew ever greater.

units.zh: 而撒改、辭不失使人告急於獵所。
units.en: Sagai and Cibushi meanwhile sent word in haste to the hunt.
units.literal: Meanwhile Sagai and Cibushi sent men to report the emergency at the hunting grounds.

units.zh: 明昌五年，贈特進，諡忠濟，與代國公歡都、特進劾者、開府儀同三司盆納、儀同三司拔達，俱配享世祖廟廷。
units.en: In Mingchang 5 he was raised to Special Advancement with the posthumous name Zhongji, Loyal and Succoring, and together with Duke of Dai Huandu, Special Advancement Hezhe, Grand Master of the Palace Penna, and Bearer of the Triple Staff Bada was granted collateral sacrifice in Shizu's temple.
units.literal: In Mingchang year 5 he was further enfeoffed as Special Advancement with the posthumous title Zhongji, "Loyal and Succoring," and together with Duke of Dai Huandu, Special Advancement Hezhe, Grand Master of the Palace with Equal Protocol Penna, and Bearer of the Triple Staff with Equal Protocol Bada, all received collateral sacrifice in Shizu's temple hall.

units.zh: 皇曾叔祖太師，機獨運心，公無私物，四方聳動，諸部歸懷，德威兩隆，風俗大定。
units.en: The imperial great-granduncle, Grand Preceptor, whose designs sprang from the heart alone and whose public service knew no private gain, stirred the four quarters until every tribe returned in allegiance; virtue and awe alike rose high, and customs were greatly settled.
units.literal: The imperial great-great-granduncle, Grand Preceptor, his machinations proceeded from the heart alone, his public-mindedness admitted no private interest; the four quarters were stirred and all tribes returned in allegiance; virtue and awe alike rose high, and customs were greatly settled.

units.zh: 申情見貌曰'穆'，博聞多能曰'憲'，柔德好眾曰'靜'，聖善周聞曰'宣'，請上皇曾叔祖太師尊諡曰穆憲皇帝，廟號肅宗，妣曰靜宣皇后。
units.en: Mu is for expressing feeling and revealing true character, xian for broad learning and many abilities, jing for gentle virtue and love of the multitude, xuan for sagely goodness known throughout the realm—we ask that the imperial great-granduncle, Grand Preceptor, receive the posthumous title Emperor Muxian, with the temple name Suzong, and that his consort be titled Empress Jingxuan.
units.literal: Mu is for expressing feeling and revealing true character, xian for broad learning and many abilities, jing for gentle virtue and love of the multitude, xuan for sagely goodness known throughout the realm—we request the posthumous honorific title Emperor Muxian for the imperial great-great-granduncle, Grand Preceptor, with the temple name Suzong, and Empress Jingxuan for his consort.

units.zh: 是歲閏十一月，增上祖宗尊諡，始祖景元皇帝曰懿憲景元皇帝，德皇帝曰淵穆玄德皇帝，安皇帝曰和靖慶安皇帝，獻祖定昭皇帝曰純烈定昭皇帝，昭祖成襄皇帝曰武惠成襄皇帝，景祖惠桓皇帝曰英烈惠桓皇帝，世祖聖肅皇帝曰神武聖肅皇帝，肅宗穆憲皇帝曰明睿穆憲皇帝，穆宗孝平皇帝曰章順孝平皇帝，康宗恭簡皇帝曰獻敏恭簡皇帝，太宗文烈皇帝曰體元應運世德昭功哲惠仁聖文烈皇帝，徽宗景宣皇帝曰允恭克讓孝德玄功佑聖景宣皇帝，已上廟號如故。
units.en: In the intercalary eleventh month of that year the court augmented the posthumous titles of the imperial ancestors: Founder Emperor Jingyuan became Emperor Yixian Jingyuan; Emperor De became Emperor Yuanmu Xuande; Emperor An became Emperor Hejing Qing'an; Xianzu Emperor Dingzhao became Emperor Chunlie Dingzhao; Zhaozu Emperor Chengxiang became Emperor Wuhui Chengxiang; Jingzu Emperor Huihuan became Emperor Yinglie Huihuan; Shizu Emperor Shengsu became Emperor Shenwu Shengsu; Suzong Emperor Muxian became Emperor Mingrui Muxian; Muzong Emperor Xiaoping became Emperor Zhangshun Xiaoping; Kangzong Emperor Gongjian became Emperor Xianmin Gongjian; Taizong Emperor Wenlie became Emperor Tiyuan Yingyun Shide Zhaogong Zhehui Rensheng Wenlie; Huizong Emperor Jingxuan became Emperor Yungong Kerang Xiaode Xuangong Yousheng Jingxuan—the temple names listed above remained unchanged.
units.literal: In the intercalary eleventh month of that year, augmented honorific titles were conferred upon the imperial ancestors: the Founder Emperor Jingyuan became Emperor Yixian Jingyuan; Emperor De became Emperor Yuanmu Xuande; Emperor An became Emperor Hejing Qing'an; Xianzu Emperor Dingzhao became Emperor Chunlie Dingzhao; Zhaozu Emperor Chengxiang became Emperor Wuhui Chengxiang; Jingzu Emperor Huihuan became Emperor Yinglie Huihuan; Shizu Emperor Shengsu became Emperor Shenwu Shengsu; Suzong Emperor Muxian became Emperor Mingrui Muxian; Muzong Emperor Xiaoping became Emperor Zhangshun Xiaoping; Kangzong Emperor Gongjian became Emperor Xianmin Gongjian; Taizong Emperor Wenlie became Emperor Tiyuan Yingyun Shide Zhaogong Zhehui Rensheng Wenlie; Huizong Emperor Jingxuan became Emperor Yungong Kerang Xiaode Xuangong Yousheng Jingxuan—the temple names above remained as before.

units.zh: 丙辰，奉上九代祖妣尊諡廟號，是日百僚上表稱賀。
units.en: On the bingchen day the court presented posthumous titles and temple names for the nine generations of ancestors and consorts; that same day the officials submitted memorials of congratulation.
units.literal: On the bingchen day, posthumous honorific titles and temple names for the nine generations of imperial ancestors and consorts were presented; on that day the hundred officials submitted memorials of congratulation.
